chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you stand in the two rak'at of the Dhuhr prayer or other than these, and you do not perform the Tashahhud in them, and you remember that in the third rak'ah before you bow (perform Ruku'), so sit down and perform the Tashahhud, and stand to complete your prayer. So if you do not remember until you have bowed, so continue in your prayer until you are finished. So when you are finished, then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdatay al-Sahw) after the greeting (Taslim), before you speak.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the Tashahhud in the first two rak'at of prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between forgetting a pillar (rukn) versus a non-pillar act, determining whether one returns to the missed component or simply completes the prayer with compensatory prostrations (sajdat al-fara'ig). The emphasis on performing the prostrations immediately after the final salam, before speaking, underscores the importance of maintaining the ritual state of worship (khushu') and preventing the nullification of the prayer's validity through casual conversation.
